I teach real estate and built-environment courses at the University of Denver,
with an emphasis on **social justice and environmental sustainability in the
built environment**. My classes lean on discussion-based learning to help
students engage deeply with the material, and I use classroom technology to give
students the chance to share their work with the world.
:::
:::

## Courses {#sec-courses}

::: {.course-grid}
::: {.course-card}
[<i class="bi bi-recycle"></i>]{.course-icon}

[REAL 1700 / 4000]{.course-code}

### Triple Bottom Line and the Built Environment

A topics course (formerly *Business of the Built Environment*) examining the
environmental, social, and economic dimensions of real estate and city building.
:::

::: {.course-card}
[<i class="bi bi-cash-coin"></i>]{.course-icon}

[REAL 3307 / 4407]{.course-code}

### Real Estate Finance / Income Property Finance

Finance and investment analysis for income-producing real estate.
:::

::: {.course-card}
[<i class="bi bi-trophy"></i>]{.course-icon}

[REAL 4800]{.course-code}

### NAIOP Rocky Mountain Real Estate Challenge

A capstone, competition-based course in which student teams develop a real
proposal for the regional NAIOP Real Estate Challenge.
:::

::: {.course-card}
[<i class="bi bi-bar-chart-line"></i>]{.course-icon}

[REAL 4701]{.course-code}

### Real Estate Market Analysis

Methods for analyzing real estate markets, demand, and submarket dynamics.
:::
:::

## Student projects {#sec-student-projects}

::: {.section-img style="background-image: url('assets/img/teach-sunset.jpg'); background-position: center 60%;"}
:::

In **Triple Bottom Line and the Built Environment**, students build public
websites around their work:

::: {.split-cards}
::: {}
[Graduate · REAL 4000]{.tag}

Students choose a critical issue related to the built environment, outline the
primary challenges, discuss how the issue affects the City of Denver, and propose
a plan of action for Denver to address it.
:::

::: {}
[Undergraduate · REAL 1700]{.tag}

Students identify a parcel of land in the Denver metro region and propose a
redevelopment — a regenerative feasibility study covering stakeholder
engagement, a theoretical LEED rating, and the financing of green enhancements.
:::
:::
